name: erlang
description: Erlang language extension for Visual Studio Code

untrustedWorkspaces.description: This extension spawns erl/rebar3 processes and runs their output, so it cannot be used safely in untrusted workspaces.

virtualWorkspaces.description: This extension needs a real filesystem to spawn erl/rebar3 against, so it does not support virtual workspaces.

arguments.description: Arguments to append erl command line.

erlpath.description: Path to the erl executable or the command if in PATH

addEbinsToCodepath.description: Add ebin directories in _build to code path

node.description: Full name of the running node to attach to, as given to -sname/-name (e.g. myapp@localhost). The node must run on this machine, with the debugger and inets OTP applications available.

cookie.description: Cookie of the node. Leave out to use ~/.erlang.cookie. Visible in the process list while attached.

cwd.description: Path of project: its .erl files are interpreted in the node

erlpath.description: Path to the erl executable used to start the helper node

configurationSnippets.description: Start erl on the project, with breakpoints in every project module

configurationSnippets.label: Erlang: Attach to a running node
configurationSnippets.description: Debug a node already running on this machine; disconnecting leaves it running

configurationSnippets.label: Erlang: Launch with the configured erl
configurationSnippets.description: Use the erl found in erlang.erlangPath (or on the PATH)

command.description: rebar3 command (compile, eunit, ct, dialyzer, release, shell, clean, ...)

args.description: Extra arguments appended after the command

profile.description: Run the command with this profile (rebar3 as <profile> <command>)

commands.title: Erlang: run eunit tests with erlang shell
Erlang: Check Erlang/OTP and rebar3 installation

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Erlang
walkthroughs.description: Set up Erlang/OTP and rebar3, then build, test and debug your first project.

steps.title: Find Erlang/OTP
steps.description:
The language server and the debugger run on your Erlang/OTP installation.
[Check installation](command:erlang.checkInstallation)
When erl is not on the PATH (kerl, asdf, custom build), point the extension to it: [Set erlang.erlangPath](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22erlang.erlangPath%22%5D)

steps.title: Pick rebar3
steps.description:
The extension looks for rebar3 in erlang.rebarPath, then in the project folder, then on the PATH, and falls back to the rebar3 bundled with the extension.
[Set erlang.rebarPath](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22erlang.rebarPath%22%5D)

media.altText: The erlang.rebarPath setting in the Settings editor

steps.title: Build the project
steps.description:
Compile with rebar3; errors and warnings land in the Problems panel. rebar3 compile, eunit, ct, dialyzer, release and shell are also available as tasks (Terminal > Run Task > rebar3).
[Build with rebar3](command:extension.rebarBuild)

media.altText: rebar3 compile output with errors listed in the Problems panel

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.description:
EUnit and Common Test tests show up in the Testing view: run, debug or run them with coverage.
[Open the Testing view](command:workbench.view.testing.focus)

media.altText: EUnit and Common Test tests in the Testing view

steps.title: Debug
steps.description:
Set a breakpoint and launch the project under the debugger, or attach to a node that is already running.
[Create a launch configuration](command:workbench.action.debug.configure)

media.altText: Debugger stopped at a breakpoint in an Erlang module

erlang.erlangPath.description: Directory where erl/escript are located. Leave empty to use default.

erlang.erlangArgs.description: Arguments passed to Erlang backend. Leave empty unless you really have to tweak the Erlang VM.

erlang.erlangDistributedNode.description: Start the Erlang backend in a distributed Erlang node. Could be useful for extension development. Note, it starts EPMD if not running yet.

erlang.rebarPath.description: Directory where rebar/rebar3 are located. Leave empty to use default.

erlang.rebarBuildArgs.description: Arguments passed to rebar/rebar3 build command.

erlang.includePaths.description: Include paths used when extension analyses the sources. Paths are read from rebar.config, and also standard set of paths is used. This setting is for special cases when the default behaviour is not enough.

erlang.linting.description: Enable/disable dynamic validation of opened Erlang source files.

erlang.cacheManagement.description: Specify where and how to store large cache tables.
enumDescriptions: Store in memory and apply lightweight compression to consume less memory (approx. 50%)

erlang.semanticTokensEnabled.description: Enable/disable semantic highlighting (module/function/macro/variable/type/record coloring computed from the real syntax tree, on top of the base TextMate grammar).

erlang.formatterEnabled.description: Enable/disable the Erlang formatter (whole-document, selection and on-type formatting).

erlang.verbose.description: Enable/disable technical traces for use in the extension development.

erlang.verboseExcludeFilter.description: List of excluded methods (i.e: textDocument/hover,textDocument/inlayHints, ...) from technical traces in the extension development.

erlang.debuggerRunMode.description: Specifies how to run vscode debugadapter. Useful in extension development.
enumDescriptions: external : launch debug adapter in separate process
server: launch debugadapter as a socket based server
inline: launch debugadapter in current process

erlang.formattingLineLength.description: Maximum line length for document formatting.
